newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures easier in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures easier in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures were easier across the board by midday on Tuesday in very thin trade as the market groped for direction in the absence of healthy buying by major consumers, dealers said.

Traders said a few hundred tonnes of the RSS1 January rubber contract was done at 176.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg. Volume yesterday in the local market was also very thin, with only 275 tonnes of the January RSS3 contract done at 124.75 U.S. cents a kg.
"Everything else was untraded. It's just a very quiet market. Buyers are staying away," a local rubber trader said.

Dealers said the market will continue drifting with weak demand likely to drag rubber prices lower in the local exchange. "I don't think the situation will change this afternoon. Rubber will remain weak," one dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, January RSS3 was indicated at 123.25 U.S. cents a kg from Monday's settlement of 124.75 cents a kg.
January RSS1 was seen at 176.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg from the previous 178.50 cents.
January TSR20 was indicated at 173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23) a kg from 174.50 cents.
